title: The release publishes everywhere by itself, and <data dir>/bin has one owner tha
input: The release publishes everywhere by itself, and <data dir>/bin has one owner that never moves back (piece 1 of 3 of 2026-11-11-004, its concepts_brief.md goals 1 and 2, decisions D-1 to D-10). The release workflow, after it creates the GitHub release, runs separate jobs, each idempotent ('already at X' is success) and re-runnable for an existing tag: it publishes the npm shim wizardingcode-mem and the OpenCode package wizardingcode-mem-opencode to npm by trusted publishing (the version from the tag, the dist-tag next for a pre-release); it renders the Homebrew formula from a template in this repository with the release's checksums and writes it into the tap homebrew-wizardingcode (the tap holds the only rendered formula); it bumps the two manifests of the marketplace wizardingcode-plugins; and it moves the image's latest tag last, after every other target succeeded. A pre-release moves none of them. The writes to the two other repositories use the fine-grained token MARKETPLACE_TOKEN, whose expiry the workflow checks and warns of a month ahead (D-9). A release that raises the team server's contract does not move the image's latest: the client side ships first and latest follows one release later, checked by the workflow (D-10). The npm shim only moves the staged binary forward (today it re-downloads whenever the versions differ, which downgrades), and wizardingcode-mem install from a channel copy never replaces a newer staged binary with an older one. A new ADR records it; the README and the release notes of the procedure follow.

criteria.text: Every pair of tests/fixtures/version-order.ts gets the same answer from olderThan (src/util/version.ts), from the generated JavaScript older() and from the shell older(); 0.9.0-rc.9 is older than 0.9.0-rc.10, and a have that is not a version is older, in all three.
The older() in npm/bin/wizardingcode-mem.js equals OLDER_JS byte for byte, and the older() block of scripts/install.sh equals the one in scripts/templates/wizardingcode-mem.sh byte for byte.

The npm shim, with a newer binary staged, downloads nothing, runs the staged binary with the arguments and exit code passed through, and prints the one line on standard error; with an older binary staged it downloads the package's version.

stageBinary keeps a staged binary of a higher version and returns it as kept; it replaces a staged binary of an equal or lower version, one that cannot be run, one that exits non-zero on --version, one whose --version output is not a version, and, with force, one of a higher version.

wizardingcode-mem install with two agents found and a newer binary staged prints the "newer … is already in" line once and hands the install over to the staged binary, which is run once with the same arguments and whose exit code is returned; with --force the staged binary is replaced by the running one, the line is absent, and both agents' hooks point at the staged path.

scripts/install.sh --download-only with a newer binary staged leaves it in place and says so; --force anywhere among the arguments replaces it; a staged file that answers something other than a version is replaced.

The formula rendered from the template with a version and a checksums.txt holds that version in every URL and each of the four checksums under its platform's block, and no mark; a checksums.txt lacking one of the four names fails, naming it.

The marketplace edit changes, in each manifest's text, only the wizardingcode-mem entry's version and ref values and leaves every other byte equal; when either manifest's entry is at a higher version it writes neither and reports it; it fails for an entry whose ref is not a version tag or that is missing.

The plan's decision refuses, each with its sentence: a ref other than refs/heads/main; a malformed tag; a tag that does not exist; a tag whose commit is not on main; a tag whose version is not its commit's package.json version; a tag whose tree lacks distribute.yml; a plain tag that is not the highest plain tag, and a pre-release tag that is not the highest tag; a release that does not exist; a draft release; a release that lacks an asset (the sentence names it); an environment release that is missing, and one whose rule is not exactly the branch main. It accepts a plain v0.9.1 while a v0.10.0-rc.1 tag exists, and for an accepted tag gives the version, the tag's commit and whether it is a pre-release. The tag list it is given holds only tags merged into main that are version tags: a v99.0.0 on a branch commit and a vnext tag change no decision.

The hold decision is "held" when the tag's lowest accepted contract is above the previous plain release's CONTRACT; "not held" when it is not, when there is no previous plain release and when the file is missing at it; "held", naming the read that failed, when the constants cannot be read at the tag and when the file is present but unreadable at the previous plain release; and "not held", marked as released by hand, when it would be held and release_hold is true. The parser's reading of the real src/team/contract.ts equals the CONTRACT and ACCEPTED_CONTRACTS the file exports.

The npm decision exits 1 for a package whose version differs from the tag's; reads a non-empty npm view answer as published, an empty answer or E404 as not published and any other failure as an error; builds npm publish --access public --ignore-scripts, with --tag next for a pre-release and without it for a plain release, and with --dry-run on a dry run; reads a publish refused because the version exists as already published; and adds the trusted-publisher sentence to an authentication failure.

The token decision maps no token, 401, 403, 404 and a 200 whose push permission is false each to its failure sentence, 200 with fewer than 30 days left to a warning, and 200 with no expiry header to an "expiry unknown" warning and a pass.

release.yml: docker's tags carry no latest; publish checks out with fetch-depth: 0; a job distribute needs publish, has actions: write, runs gh workflow run distribute.yml --ref main with the tag, and its run: holds no ${{.

distribute.yml: the only trigger is workflow_dispatch with tag, dry_run and release_hold; top-level permissions is empty; one concurrency group, not cancelled; every job runs on ubuntu-latest with timeout-minutes: 15; npm, tap and marketplace name the environment release and plan and latest name none; only npm has id-token: write and only latest has packages: write; the run is named distribute <tag>; latest needs plan, npm, tap and marketplace; tap, marketplace and latest are conditioned on a plain release, latest on no hold and on not being cancelled, with a first step that fails when a needed job did not succeed, and latest's retag step on no dry run; npm's checkout of the release's tree takes its ref from plan's sha output, and no checkout takes inputs.tag.

In distribute.yml, no run: script contains ${{; every uses: is pinned to a 40-character commit SHA; every actions/checkout has persist-credentials: false; and secrets.MARKETPLACE_TOKEN appears exactly four times, each in the env: of a step of the jobs tap and marketplace.

The writer to another repository, run against a local bare repository: an unchanged tree makes no commit and reports "already at"; a changed tree makes one commit wizardingcode-mem <version> and pushes it; a push refused as not fast-forward succeeds after one rebase; a dry run leaves the remote as it was; the git commands and remote URL it builds carry no token, which travels only in the child's environment; and, given a commit the tag no longer names, it refuses before any write, for a lightweight and for an annotated tag.

summaryLine gives, for each target and outcome of the summary table, exactly that text, the token's three lines, a failed target's line, the plan's refusal and the "not moved" line included; plan writes the three "skipped: pre-release" lines for a pre-release, the "held" line for a hold and its refusal line when it refuses.

docs/runbooks/release.md holds the one-time setup in its order (the ruleset on main checked, with one approval to require once a second person has write access; the ruleset on v* tags; the environment's rule before the secret and any secret found there removed; the token with its date noted; the two trusted publishers), the first release's order (the refused automatic run, the dry run and what it does not prove, the real dispatch), what a run shows, the repeat, the repairs (a release that lacks an asset; a tag whose release failed, which blocks the repeat of the release before it; each of the four external writes' failure message), the way back (install --force; a bad release is fixed by a higher version; do not re-run a run whose write was reverted by hand), the release of a hold, and the limits (a third dispatch replaces a pending one; the dist-tag next; shims already published; the release's assets are not tied to the judged commit, with making releases immutable where the repository's settings offer it; latest can be moved outside the workflow).
docs/runbooks/team-server.md says latest moves last and may be held, and cites the release runbook.

docs/adr/0029-release-distribution.md records the decisions D-1 to D-5 and those carried from 2026-11-11-004, the alternatives and the limits, including that a staged file answering a very high version is replaced only by --force, and that it supersedes the Homebrew row of ADR 0008.
CLAUDE.md names the two workflows, the scripts under scripts/release/, the environment, the forward-only rule with install --force, the runbook and the ADR.

tests/unit/release-docs.test.ts holds the release's documents to the code: the team runbook and CLAUDE.md cite docs/runbooks/release.md; CLAUDE.md names the two workflows, scripts/release/lib.ts, ADR 0029, install --force and the environment release; every wizardingcode-mem command the release runbook cites is one the CLI knows, with a flag its module names; every repository file it cites exists; and the lines of its 'What a run shows' section are exactly the lines summaryLine can write, none left out.

decisions.question: The workflow's shape: one release.yml with a plan job and a workflow_dispatch repeat, or release.yml as it is starting a separate dispatch-only distribute.yml (npm, tap, marketplace, latest) whose token and npm publish sit under a GitHub environment 'release' restricted to main?
decisions.default: The separate distribute.yml under the environment 'release': no skip conditions that fail green, and a dispatch from an edited branch cannot reach the token or the npm publish.
decisions.answer: The separate distribute.yml: release.yml as it is, starting a dispatch-only distribute.yml with the tag; the token and the npm publish under a GitHub environment 'release' restricted to main. (the person, 2026-11-12: chose 'distribute.yml separado e protegido', the default)

decisions.question: Where the contract rule for the image's latest lives and what it tests: in piece 3 with the server's upgrader; in this piece corrected (latest held when the release's lowest accepted contract is above the previous plain release's CONTRACT, with a dispatch input that releases the hold); or in this piece as D-10 of 2026-11-11-004 worded it (held on any rise of CONTRACT until the next release)?
decisions.default: In piece 3, with the upgrader that reads latest; this piece only moves latest last and never lower.
decisions.answer: In this piece, corrected: latest is held when the release's lowest accepted contract is above the previous plain release's CONTRACT, with a dispatch input that releases the hold. (the person, 2026-11-12: chose 'Já na peça 1, corrigida', against the default)

decisions.question: The weekly scheduled check of the token (token.yml, door.ts): keep it with its limits written, or remove it and leave the check on the release run (a named failure, a warning under 30 days) with GitHub's own expiry email and the date noted at creation as the advance notice?
decisions.default: Keep the weekly check, with its limits written (D-9 of 2026-11-11-004 asked for a warning a month ahead).
decisions.answer: Remove the weekly check: the release run's check stays (a named failure, a warning under 30 days); the advance notice is GitHub's expiry email and the date noted when the token is created. (the person, 2026-11-12: chose 'Retirar a verificação semanal', against the default)

decisions.question: A ruleset that reserves creating, updating and deleting v* tags to admins: a mandatory step of the one-time setup, or an optional suggestion in the runbook?
decisions.default: Mandatory: it is the second barrier behind the workflow's own checks, and the only one for the image's latest.
decisions.answer: Mandatory in the one-time setup; the workflow still checks that the tag is on main and counts only tags on main. (the person, 2026-11-12: chose 'Obrigatório', the default)

decisions.question: The ruleset on main requires a pull request and three status checks but zero approvals (read 2026-11-12): write that limit into the spec and the runbook (the barrier is a pull request with green checks; require one approval when a second person has write access), or require one approval now as a setup step?
decisions.default: Write the limit; require an approval when a second person has write access.
decisions.answer: Write the limit: the barrier is a pull request with green checks, which stops access from a branch or a tag, not someone who can merge to main; the runbook says to require one approval when a second person has write access. (the person, 2026-11-12: chose 'Escrever o limite', the default)
